summary: The flake fix, the alert-helper unification, and the migration hardening are all verified solid and ready as-is. The video rule's F1/F2 fix is a real, well-tested correction of the round-1 blocker (independently re-verified with a 13-case matrix plus the author's own pinned 9-row test, all pass) -- but probing the same class of risk the round-1 test-reviewer used (idiomatic English around the newly-freed lead word) found that the fix ITSELF reopens a sibling false-drop: 'Watch' followed by a determiner/possessive/quantifier ('this', 'that', 'these', 'those', 'our', 'my', 'all', 'every') now unconditionally drops via the new subject-position noun-phrase branch, even though none of those sentences are about video content -- e.g. 'Watch this space for more Treasure Hunt reveals coming soon' and 'Watch these five castings before they vanish from pegs' (a near-restatement of the class the round-1 fix explicitly says it protects, 'watch out for these five Treasure Hunts'). No pinned test exercises 'watch' + a determiner, so this shipped invisibly. Recommend narrowing branch (A2) so 'watch' only qualifies via the separator form (A1, 'Watch: ...'), before this ships.

priority_1_flake_fix.root_cause_matches_symptom: Confirmed against my own round-1 observation: the flake only reproduced when TestResolveHoldCallback/TestReviewCallbackGrammarsCoexist ran in the same process as TestReviewListener::test_review_listener_dispatches_admin_cancel, and never in isolation or in 300 in-process repeats of a single test -- exactly the signature of a leaked module attribute from an EARLIER test's aborted tearDown, not a race inside the hold-callback code itself. The fix targets the actual mechanism (sequential tearDown -> addCleanup) rather than papering over symptoms.
priority_1_flake_fix.non_vacuity_check: Mutated tests/test_integration.py's _IntegrationBase back to the pre-fix sequential setUp/tearDown pattern (7 patchers via .start(), one tearDown with 7 sequential .stop() calls, no addCleanup) and re-ran TestIntegrationBaseCleanupIsolation: all 3 guard tests failed with 8 subtest failures total (DB_FILE/TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN/TELEGRAM_CHANNEL_ID/TELEGRAM_ADMIN_ID/SOURCES/fetch_mattel_news/send_admin_notification all reported as leaked), confirming the guard is a real regression detector, not a vacuous pass. Reverted via `git checkout -- tests/test_integration.py` immediately after (working tree confirmed clean before and after).
priority_1_flake_fix.lifo_ordering: Traced test_a_subclass_re_arming_via_addcleanup_pairs_correctly by hand against the actual registration order in _IntegrationBase.setUp (8 registrations: _unlink_db, then _stop_quietly for db/token/channel/admin/notify/mattel/sources patchers in that order) plus the inner _ReArming class's 2 extra registrations (notify.start, then nothing else). LIFO execution order places notify.start (registered 9th) BEFORE the base's _stop_quietly(notify_patcher) (registered 6th) in the reversed execution sequence, so notify_patcher ends the test correctly STOPPED, not left running -- matches the test's own assertion and my trace confirms the mechanism, not just the outcome.
priority_1_flake_fix.backward_compat_with_old_teardown_subcla: 5 classes in the file still define an explicit tearDown (TestOutageStateIntegration ~L546, plus 3 others), unmodified by this commit. Verified TestOutageStateIntegration's pattern (stop notify_patcher in setUp, start it + call super().tearDown() in its own tearDown) still works: unittest always runs tearDown() before doCleanups(), so the subclass's manual notify_patcher.start() executes before the base's addCleanup-registered _stop_quietly(notify_patcher) fires -- pairing holds regardless of LIFO, because tearDown-vs-cleanups ordering is a stronger guarantee than cleanup-vs-cleanup LIFO. Ran this class plus TestCrashLoopGuard/TestPublishRecapIntegration/TestInFlightCancelGuard (the other old-tearDown classes): 14 passed.
priority_1_flake_fix.no_cleanup_silently_skipped: Diffed the old tearDown body against the new setUp's addCleanup registrations line by line: same 7 patcher stops plus the db unlink, same relative ordering preserved (db/token/channel/admin/notify/mattel/sources -> now registered in that order and executed LIFO-reversed, db unlink still last). Nothing dropped, nothing added beyond the SchemaMigrationError-adjacent stub work covered separately.

priority_2_unified_alert_helpers.method: Checked out the pre-refactor commit (98cadd7) into a scratch git worktree, ran admin_alerts.alert_promo_blocked with 3 inputs (realistic promo title+markers, a 500-char pathological title with empty markers, and a non-str title with a non-str marker) against both the old inline logic and the new commit's _intake_alert_title/_intake_alert_markers-based version, and diffed the repr() output byte-for-byte -- IDENTICAL across all 3 cases. The only behavioral difference between old and new marker-rendering is that the new _intake_alert_markers coerces each marker to str via a generator (`str(m) for m in markers`) inside a try/except, versus the old bare `", ".join(markers)` with no guard -- a difference that only matters for a markers list containing a non-str element, which never occurs in production (promo_markers/hold_markers/genre_markers are always list[str] of the module's own marker constants). Existing test_admin_alerts.py was not modified by this commit at all (git diff empty) and still passes unchanged (114 passed, 8 subtests) -- itself evidence the refactor is output-preserving, since those tests assert on exact alert text.
priority_2_unified_alert_helpers.cleanup: Worktree removed after the comparison; tests/test_integration.py mutation from the flake check was already reverted separately.

priority_3_migration_refactor.readability: Clear three-function shape (_column_exists / _ensure_column / _COLUMN_MIGRATIONS tuple + loop) replaces a bare try/except-in-a-for-loop with named, independently testable steps. Each _COLUMN_MIGRATIONS entry keeps its original historical comment (2026-04-30, 2026-06-XX, 2026-07-25) so the audit trail from the pre-refactor code is not lost.
priority_3_migration_refactor.correctness_of_check_alter_verify: Confirmed the three-step sequence is genuinely exercised, not decorative: tests/test_database.py's two pre-existing mocked-connection tests (test_init_db_creates_all_tables, test_init_db_also_creates_pending_tables) BROKE against a bare MagicMock once this landed -- MagicMock's default __iter__ yields nothing, so the pre-ALTER existence check reports every column missing, the ALTER is attempted (no-op success on a mock), and the POST-alter verification then also reports the column missing and raises SchemaMigrationError. The commit correctly added _stub_schema_probe to make those two tests report all migrated columns as pre-existing. This is exactly the signal a reviewer wants: the verify step is not dead code, it actively fires when its precondition (ALTER did nothing) is met. Independently confirmed `SELECT name FROM pragma_table_info(?)` with a bound table-name parameter actually works against the project's sqlite3 (3.46.1) with a quick standalone script.
priority_3_migration_refactor.error_typing: SchemaMigrationError(RuntimeError) is a sensible choice -- callers that don't specifically expect it still catch it via `except Exception`/`except RuntimeError` elsewhere in the codebase without a new import, while `except sqlite3.OperationalError` (the pre-refactor implicit contract) correctly no longer swallows it. `duplicate column name` is matched case-insensitively as the ONE tolerated OperationalError; the error path logs at ERROR with table/column/exception type before raising (`from exc` preserves the chain), and the post-ALTER verification failure path is a distinct log line + raise for the 'should be unreachable' case. Both paths are tested against a REAL SQLite IMMEDIATE lock (tests/test_pending_articles_repo.py::TestColumnMigrationHardening, not a mocked exception) -- ran this class: 18 passed, including test_a_swallowed_lock_would_break_the_publish_path, which pins the actual severity argument (count_pending/list_pending/list_held all raise `no such column: hold_reason` once the column is genuinely missing), test_duplicate_column_race_is_still_tolerated, and test_verification_catches_an_alter_that_did_not_take (a fake connection whose ALTER silently no-ops).
priority_3_migration_refactor.pragma_call: `SELECT name FROM pragma_table_info(?)` -- using the table-valued-function form specifically to bind the table name via `?` rather than string-formatting it into `PRAGMA table_info(x)` is the correct call here and matches the module's existing SQL-audit discipline (TestSqlAudit forbids string-interpolated SQL). No injection surface: table/column arguments to _ensure_column all come from the module-level _COLUMN_MIGRATIONS tuple, never caller/request data.
priority_3_migration_refactor.callers_unaffected: init_db() (news_bot.py) does not catch exceptions from pending_repo.init_schema, so a genuine SchemaMigrationError propagates to whichever caller invoked init_db() (main() at startup, or job() on every tick) and crashes loudly -- this is the intended 'fail loudly and early' behavior per the docstring, and is a strict improvement over the old silent-pass failure mode (which would eventually surface as a confusing `no such column` deep inside list_pending/count_pending on some LATER tick, with no log line pointing at the migration). Not flagged as an issue; it's the point of the change.

priority_4_video_rule_quality.readability_and_maintainability: The branch-A/branch-B split (subject position vs. two independent signals) is well-named and the marker tables are cleanly layered: _GENRE_VIDEO_MARKERS (anywhere) -> _GENRE_VIDEO_LEAD_ONLY_MARKERS ('watch', deliberately excluded from the anywhere set) -> _GENRE_VIDEO_LEAD_MARKERS (union, feeds the lead regexes) -> _GENRE_VIDEO_REVIEW_MARKERS (the second-signal co-markers). The longest-first sorting in _GENRE_VIDEO_LEAD_ALT (so 'vídeos' wins over 'vídeo' in the alternation) is a real, load-bearing detail, correctly implemented and verified live ('Vídeos: revela dois Porsches raros' -> ('video', ['vídeos:', 'vídeos']), not a truncated/broken match). test_no_review_marker_contains_a_video_marker and test_np_heads_contain_no_verbs_that_would_reopen_the_fp are exactly the right structural-invariant tests to have (mirrors the promo filter's own round-1 double-count lesson, cited explicitly in the code comments).
priority_4_video_rule_quality.verification_matrix: Independently re-ran a 13-case matrix covering all round-1 F1/F2 examples plus the operator's required-drop cases plus the event rule (untouched) -- 13/13 match expected classification. Then ran the author's own pinned tests/test_relevance_filter.py::TestVideoRuleVerificationMatrix (4 MUST_NOT_DROP + 5 MUST_DROP = 9 rows, matching the commit message's '9-row verification matrix' claim) plus TestIsRejectedGenre: 27 passed. F1/F2 are genuinely fixed: 'Mattel drops video revealing the 2027 Corvette Z06...', 'Vídeo revela o novo Porsche 911 GT3 RS...', and 'Unboxing surprises us: ... Supra revealed' all now correctly classify as (None, []) -- confirmed live, not just via the test suite.
priority_4_video_rule_quality.comment_accuracy_vs_behaviour: One inaccuracy found: the docstring's branch-B example 'two DISTINCT genre words ("Assista ao unboxing …")' is misleading -- I traced this example and it is actually resolved by branch A (subject position, NP-head form: 'assista' + 'ao', where 'ao' is a listed determiner/preposition), returning before branch B is ever evaluated. Branch B's two-distinct-genre-words path IS independently reachable (verified with 'Check the full video unboxing here for the 2027 lineup' -> ('video', ['vídeo', 'unboxing']), which is NOT in lead position), just not by the example given in the docstring. Cosmetic, not a logic bug -- low severity, listed as a finding below.

findings.issue: The subject-position NP-head branch (A2), designed to let 'Unboxing THE 2026 H case' and 'Assista AO ...' count as subject-position without requiring a colon, was applied to 'watch' as well -- but 'watch' is fundamentally different from 'vídeo'/'unboxing'/'assista' in this context: those are effectively NOUNS heading a noun-phrase headline, while 'watch' is an ordinary IMPERATIVE VERB, and 'Watch [determiner] [noun]' is indistinguishable from ordinary English regardless of topic. Because _GENRE_VIDEO_NP_HEADS includes demonstratives/possessives/quantifiers ('this', 'that', 'these', 'those', 'our', 'my', 'all', 'every'), any sentence of the shape 'Watch {this|that|these|those|our|my|all|every} ...' now drops unconditionally, with NO video content required. Reproduced live (all four DROP, none are about video): 'Watch this space for more Treasure Hunt reveals coming soon', 'Watch these five castings before they vanish from pegs', 'Watch our shelves fill up with the new J case this week', 'Watch all the new castings drop this fall'. The second of these is a near-restatement of the EXACT sentence the round-1 fix's own code comment cites as the risk to avoid ('watch out for these five Treasure Hunts on pegs this month' — MUST_NOT_DROP case #4 in the pinned matrix) -- it just swaps 'out for' for 'these', and the new branch drops it anyway. No test in TestVideoRuleVerificationMatrix or elsewhere exercises 'watch' followed by a determiner/possessive/quantifier, so this shipped without a red test. Same consequence class as the original F1/F2: DROP is permanent, no operator visibility, no recovery.
findings.fix: Narrow branch (A2) so 'watch' only ever qualifies via the separator form (A1, 'Watch: ...', 'Watch - ...'), not the NP-head form -- i.e. exclude _GENRE_VIDEO_LEAD_ONLY_MARKERS from the NP-head regex's alternation while keeping it in the separator regex's alternation (two alternations instead of one shared _GENRE_VIDEO_LEAD_ALT, or a second smaller ALT built from _GENRE_VIDEO_MARKERS only for the NP form). Verified this would not break the pinned 9-row matrix: none of the MUST_DROP rows rely on 'watch' + an NP head (the only 'Watch' row uses the colon/separator form). Alternatively, if the NP-head form must stay unified for maintainability, drop 'this'/'that'/'these'/'those'/'our'/'my'/'all'/'every' from _GENRE_VIDEO_NP_HEADS entirely and rely on the closed set of true articles/prepositions ('the', 'a', 'an', 'of', 'with') plus the PT list, which are far less likely to head an ordinary imperative sentence.

findings.issue: The docstring's branch-B example 'two DISTINCT genre words ("Assista ao unboxing …")' is not actually resolved by branch B -- traced and confirmed it is caught by branch A (subject position, NP-head form via 'assista' + 'ao') and returns before branch B is evaluated. The docstring's characterization of this specific example is inaccurate, though the underlying two-distinct-genre-words mechanism in branch B is real and independently reachable by other inputs (verified: 'Check the full video unboxing here for the 2027 lineup', not in lead position, correctly triggers branch B alone).
findings.fix: Replace the docstring's branch-B example with one that is not ALSO caught by branch A, e.g. a genre word appearing later in the title alongside another genre word or a review co-marker, so the example actually demonstrates the code path it's attached to.
